MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L31·N3175unmasked layer
Rather than a lexical detector, this neuron gives broad low-level activation across informal user-generated comment/review prose, peaking on mid-clause continuation words (determiners/adverbs/adjectives like "this", "that", "then", "all", "fantastic", "member"); it is strongly *suppressed* by paragraph-initial question/clause openers such as "How" or "In" that start a new rhetorical sentence after a newline.

L31·N12222unmasked layer
This neuron has no single lexical trigger; it fires diffusely across fluent expository prose, peaking on mid-sentence function/linking words that sit just before their complement (e.g. "would" before "not consider", "of" before "vouchers", "by" before "their keepers", "often" before "necessary", "offer" before "protection"), and is strongly suppressed on other similar mid-sentence connectives/auxiliaries ("to", "since", "will", "Successfully") — i.e. it looks like a next-token-prediction/context neuron rather than a semantic detector.
